name: Load Testing Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any load testing task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any load testing task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about load testing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. When multiple load testing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Before starting load testing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to load testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Check that load testing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen load testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. When load testing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Keep load testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
9. Keep load testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. Validate load testing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. Prefer the simplest load testing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
12. Prefer explicit, readable load testing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of load testing correctness.
- Do not apply generic load testing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting load testing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop load testing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new load testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about load testing over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
